name: Cognizant
summary: Cognizant hires most freshers in India through GenC (Generation Cognizant), which it describes as its hiring and development programme for emerging talent, via campus and off-campus drives. It says its assessments evaluate communication skills, aptitude and/or technical skills depending on the role, and candidates commonly report a technical and an HR interview after them, centred on fundamentals, SQL and their own projects.
looks_for: Fundamentals: OOP, DBMS, SQL, a language

questions.text: Tell me about yourself.
covers: Your degree and the technologies you know best
One project and your part in it, with a result
Why you're applying for this role, in under two minutes

questions.text: Write a SQL query to find the second-highest salary.
covers: A subquery: the highest salary that is below MAX(salary)
Or DENSE_RANK in a window function, which also handles ties and the Nth highest
What happens with duplicate salaries, nulls, or fewer than two rows

questions.text: Explain your project's architecture.
covers: The layers: front end, back end, database and any outside services
How one request flows through them, using a single feature as the example
Why you chose that design and what you'd change now

questions.text: Are you comfortable relocating?
covers: A clear, honest answer, with any real constraint stated politely
Why you're open to it, such as the projects and learning it brings
Anything that shows you've adapted before, like studying away from home

questions.text: Tell me about a time your team succeeded because people relied on each other's strengths.
covers: Who did what, and why the split suited each person
How you helped someone or asked for help yourself
What the team achieved that one person couldn't have

questions.text: Tell me about a time you took ownership of a problem that wasn't strictly yours.
covers: The problem and why nobody had picked it up
What you did and who you kept informed
The outcome, and whether you'd step in the same way again

questions.text: Tell me about a time you tried a new approach instead of the usual one. Did it work?
covers: The usual way and what was wrong with it
The new approach and how you tested it safely
The result, including what didn't work

questions.text: What's a piece of feedback that changed how you work?
covers: The feedback, who gave it and why it stung or surprised you
What you changed in practice
How you know the change is working

questions.text: Explain the difference between DELETE, TRUNCATE and DROP in SQL.
covers: DELETE removes chosen rows and can be filtered with WHERE
TRUNCATE empties the whole table quickly but keeps its structure
DROP removes the table itself; how rollback and triggers differ between them

questions.text: What is the difference between method overloading and method overriding? Give an example.
covers: Overloading: same name, different parameters, chosen at compile time
Overriding: a subclass replaces a parent method, chosen at run time
A short example, such as area() for shapes or a payment's process() method

questions.text: A page in your project takes ten seconds to load. How would you find out why?
covers: Measuring first: browser network tools, server logs, query times
Common causes: slow database queries, large images or scripts, too many calls
One fix, and how you'd check it actually helped

questions.text: For experienced candidates: how have you handled a client who changed requirements late in a release?
covers: Understanding why the change mattered to the client
Showing the impact on scope, dates and risk clearly
The agreement reached and how the team delivered it

questions.text: Why Cognizant, and what kind of work would you like to do here?
covers: Something specific: the GenC training path, a practice area, or recent work you read about
The kind of projects or technologies you'd like to start with
How that fits your longer-term plan

questions.text: Do you have any questions for us?
covers: One or two thoughtful questions about training, the first project or the team
Nothing already answered on the careers site
A brief thank-you

tips: Revise SQL joins and simple queries.
Be ready to explain every technology on your resume.
Read the GenC page for the track you're applying to; the role decides whether assessments lean on aptitude, coding or communication.
Practise explaining a SQL query out loud: what each clause does and the order it runs in.
Keep a short story ready for a few of Cognizant's values, such as owning a problem or trying a new approach.
Keep your resume and academic certificates ready; Cognizant asks for them during hiring.
